Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: single front-view 3D character modeling reference for Meshy, CATHEXIS from Loopforge.
Input image 1 is the authoritative original character sheet; image 2 supplies costume and material detail. Preserve her identity closely. Render ONE full-body character, straight-on orthographic FRONT, neutral symmetric A-pose: arms 35 degrees off torso, elbows straight, palms forward, five individually separated mechanical fingers on each hand, feet hip-width apart flat on the same plane. Plain mid-gray studio background, large subject with margin, no text, no inset views, no props, no smoke, no bloom. Neutral soft lighting, rich crisp physically plausible materials and restrained painted-comic detail.
CATHEXIS is a theatrical porcelain-and-brass robot diva. Retain slender elegant mature humanoid proportions, mechanical high-heeled feet, cracked ivory chest and shoulder plates, black articulated corset structure with antique brass ribs, exposed dark joint mechanisms, amber glass canisters at the hips, a brass headset/crown like a small industrial diadem (not a giant fantasy crown), and grouped cable-hair swept behind shoulders.
CRITICAL PRODUCTION CHANGE: the removable porcelain face mask is NOT attached in this body reference. Show her compact dark metal facial understructure with the two recessed amber eye emitters, small mechanical jaw/speaker teeth, and a thin oval perimeter seating rim on forehead, temples and chin. It must fit beneath a later beautiful faceplate; do not enlarge the skull, do not make a skeletal horror monster, do not add a human skin face. Crown, ears and head remain intact.
Keep her distinctive layered distressed ivory-gray skirt, but make it an OPEN FRONT overdress split into broad left/right/rear hanging panels, attached at hips, hanging naturally without wind. Clear open gap from upper thighs to feet showing BOTH mechanical legs and their full separation; no fabric between thighs, no cloth fused to hands or legs. Ragged panel hems terminate around upper calves, no floor-length train, no veil of wispy transparent threads. A small fitted waist drape is okay but must not hide hip separation. Preserve theatrical richness using a few broad fabric shapes and painted textile detail, not a shapeless skirt blob.
No weapons, no syringes, no tools held in hands, no wings, no added body text. Detailed believable robot construction, not smooth toy shapes. This is a rigging reference, so do not give her a seductive contrapposto or asymmetrical performance pose; personality comes from design.

Use case: stylized-concept. Cable-hair is grouped into broad wavy locks routed down left and right of the cage so it remains visible, no floating flyaways. Brass corset ribs continue around waist. Ragged ivory-gray overskirt consists of separate broad draped rear/side panels to upper calves, not a fused cone; it leaves ankles and articulated heels visible. Include a long central rear slit so leg separation is readable. Keep porcelain shoulder and forearm plates. No extra faces, masks, weapons, text, inset diagrams or perspective angle. Do not turn the head, do not pose one leg ahead. This image must be recognizably the back of the same character and same costume.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: CATHEXIS removable mask model reference. Use original character sheet input 1 as identity authority, and the maskless generated body input 2 for seating fit. ONE isolated rigid porcelain FACEPLATE, almost front view with only a slight 12-degree three-quarter angle so thin shell thickness is evident. It is a face mask from forehead to chin, not a whole head: NO scalp, ears, crown, hair, neck, eyeballs, straps, stand or handle. Feminine elegant mature face matching the original CATHEXIS, long oval, fine high cheekbones, straight nose, subtly warm small CLOSED smile conveying 'Trust me, darling', calm lifted brows and open almond eye holes. Weathered ivory ceramic, fine dark crazing, discreet warm tarnished brass rim and two tiny temple latch seats. Thin hollow concave shell with believable shallow volume; the eye openings are actual holes, not glowing eyeballs. Back interior only glimpsed at edge. Do not make a solid bust or flat paper mask. Tasteful uncanny beauty, restrained cracked porcelain, not a cartoon happy emoji, no exaggerated comedy mask, no tears. Isolated centered on neutral mid-gray, studio soft lighting, ultra-clear contours, no text or diagrams. This is mask 01 'Grace', the default public face.

Do not zoom or crop or add a second image. Input 2 is the original character sheet showing the mechanical grimace beneath porcelain. Clearly one head with two contrasting halves, not a little chipped cheek. Original character-sheet split-face motif made bold. The exposed side's grimace and the calm porcelain side should visibly disagree.
